lesson_title: The Morning That Changed the War
hook_text: It was 7:55 on a Sunday morning in Hawaii. A radar operator saw the planes coming. He was told not to worry.
clip_script: Sunday, 7 December 1941. Pearl Harbour, Hawaii. Sailors are asleep or dressing for church. Out at sea, six Japanese aircraft carriers have crept across the ocean in radio silence. Why? Oil. Japan had almost none, America had cut off supply, and Japan's leaders decided to take the oil of South-East Asia by force. First they had to knock out the American navy. At 7:55 the bombs fall. In two hours, eight battleships are hit, the Arizona explodes, and 2 403 Americans die. But the American carriers are not there. They are out at sea. The next day, President Roosevelt calls it a date which will live in infamy. America declares war. Four days later Hitler declares war on America. Japan wins for six months. Then, at Midway, it loses four carriers in one day. A brilliant surprise. A terrible mistake.
visual_style: A calm harbour at dawn; a radar screen with blips; planes in two waves across a map of the Pacific; a fuel gauge dropping to empty over a map of Japan; a newspaper headline with the date 7 December 1941; four carrier icons sinking at Midway.
pacing: Quiet opening, sudden fast cuts for the attack, steady close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand why Japan attacked and why it changed the whole war.
